question: Define: Mineral
answer: A naturally occurring, inorganic crystalline solid with a definite chemical composition and ordered internal atomic structure.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Silicate Tetrahedron [SiO4]4-
answer: Fundamental building block. 1 silicon ion surrounded by 4 oxygen ions in tetrahedral coordination.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Bond types
answer: Covalent (strong, directional, e.g. diamond/quartz), Ionic (transfer of electrons, moderate strength, e.g. halite), Metallic (electron sea, high conductivity, e.g. pyrite), van der Waals (weak intermolecular, cleavage planes in graphite/mica).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Isolated tetrahedra
answer: Olivine (Mg,Fe)2SiO4. No cleavage, fracture only. High density.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Single chains
answer: Augite / Pyroxene. Chains bonded by cations. Two cleavage planes intersecting at 90° (87°/93°).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Double chains
answer: Hornblende / Amphibole. Two cleavage planes intersecting at 60° and 120° (56°/124°).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Sheet silicates
answer: Micas (Biotite / Muscovite). Tetrahedra share 3 oxygens. One perfect basal cleavage.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: 3D Framework
answer: Quartz (SiO2) - shares all 4 oxygens, no cleavage, conchoidal fracture. Feldspars (Orthoclase / Plagioclase) - 2 cleavages at ~90°.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Hardness (Mohs scale)
answer: Talc(1) < Gypsum(2) < [Fingernail ~2.5] < Calcite(3) < [Copper ~3.5] < Fluorite(4) < Apatite(5) < [Steel/Glass ~5.5] < Orthoclase(6) < Quartz(7) < Topaz(8) < Corundum(9) < Diamond(10).

question: Compare and distinguish: Calcite vs Quartz
answer: Calcite scratches with copper/nail (H=3), effervesces with dilute cold HCl (CaCO3 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + H2O + CO2), 3 directions of rhombohedral cleavage. Quartz scratches glass (H=7), no acid reaction, conchoidal fracture.

question: State the key Thin section optical properties:
Diagnostic Properties (Hand Specimen & Thin Section): key facts
answer: • Plane polarised light (PPL): Relief (refractive index vs resin), Pleochroism (colour change on rotation e.g. Biotite brown-yellow, Hornblende green-brown), Cleavage traces.

question: Diagnostic Properties (Hand Specimen & Thin Section): key facts
answer: • Crossed polars (XPL): Birefringence / Interference colours (order of colours on Michel-Lévy chart), Extinction angle (straight/parallel in quartz/orthoclase/biotite, inclined in augite/hornblende), Twinning (cross-hatched in microcline, albite polysynthetic stripes in plagioclase, Carlsbad simple twin in orthoclase).

question: Goldich Weathering Series & Stability: key facts
answer: Minerals that crystallise at the highest temperatures and pressures (least like surface conditions) weather the fastest.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Susceptibility to chemical weathering
answer: Olivine (fastest) > Augite > Hornblende > Biotite > Plagioclase > Orthoclase > Muscovite > Quartz (most resistant).

question: Goldich Weathering Series & Stability: key facts
answer: Quartz and clays dominate mature sedimentary deposits because quartz is mechanically hard and chemically inert.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Mechanical weathering
answer: Freeze-thaw (9% water expansion in joints), Exfoliation / onion-skin (insolation thermal expansion/contraction in arid climates), Salt crystallisation.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Chemical weathering
Weathering & Transport: key facts
answer: • Carbonation: Rainwater dissolves CO2 -> carbonic acid (H2CO3) dissolving limestone.

question: Weathering & Transport: key facts
answer: • Hydrolysis: Acidified water attacks feldspar -> kaolinite (china clay) + silicic acid + soluble K+/Na+ ions.

question: Weathering & Transport: key facts
answer: • Oxidation: Iron minerals (e.g. olivine, augite, pyrite) react with oxygen -> hematite / limonite (rust red).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Hjulström Curve
answer: Relates sediment grain size to water flow velocity required for erosion (entrainment), transport, and deposition.

question: Weathering & Transport: key facts
answer: • Clay/silt requires higher velocity to entrain than sand due to electrostatic cohesion.

question: Weathering & Transport: key facts
answer: • Sand entrains at the lowest velocity (~20 cm/s).

question: Weathering & Transport: key facts
answer: • Deposition occurs whenever velocity drops below settling velocity.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Grain size (Wentworth scale)
answer: Gravel / Rudaceous (>2 mm), Sand / Arenaceous (0.0625 mm - 2 mm), Mud / Argillaceous (<0.0625 mm, silt and clay).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Textural maturity
answer: Increases with transport distance and time: Poorly sorted + angular + high matrix -> Well sorted + well rounded + low matrix (orthoquartzite).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Clastic rock types
Textural Maturity & Clastic Classification: key facts
answer: • Breccia: Angular clasts (>2 mm), near-source deposit (scree / fault talus / wadi flash flood).

question: Textural Maturity & Clastic Classification: key facts
answer: • Conglomerate: Rounded clasts (>2 mm), high-energy aqueous transport (beach / high-energy river channel).

question: Textural Maturity & Clastic Classification: key facts
answer: • Orthoquartzite: >95% quartz grains, well rounded, well sorted, silica cement; high-energy shallow marine / beach.

question: Textural Maturity & Clastic Classification: key facts
answer: • Arkose: >25% feldspar, pink/red, moderate sorting/rounding; rapid deposition from granitic source in semi-arid alluvial fan.

question: Textural Maturity & Clastic Classification: key facts
answer: • Greywacke: Poorly sorted, angular grains in dark fine-grained muddy matrix (>15%); submarine turbidity current deposit.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Cross-bedding
answer: Formed by migrating ripples/dunes. Asymptotic curve at base, sharp truncation at top by erosion. Way-up: Tops truncated. Paleocurrent: Dips down-current.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Graded bedding
answer: Coarse clasts at base fining upward into fine silt/mud (density current / turbidity current settling). Way-up: Coarse at base, fine at top.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Asymmetrical ripples
answer: Formed by unidirectional current (river, wind); steep lee slope down-current.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Symmetrical ripples
answer: Formed by bidirectional oscillatory wave action in shallow water; sharp crests point up.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Desiccation mudcracks
answer: V-shaped cracks in mud due to subaerial drying; V points downwards.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Oolitic limestone
answer: Formed of spherical ooids (calcite precipitated concentrically around nucleus in warm, agitated, supersaturated shallow marine water).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Bioclastic limestone
answer: Abundant fossil fragments (crinoids, bivalves, corals) cemented by sparry calcite.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Chalk
answer: Pure white micrite of microscopic coccolith plates (calcareous nannoplankton) in quiet pelagic marine shelf.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Evaporites
answer: Halite (NaCl), Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O), Anhydrite. Sequential precipitation in restricted marine basins with high evaporation > precipitation.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Diagenesis stages
Carbonate & Chemical Sediments & Diagenesis: key facts
answer: 1. Compaction: Expulsion of pore water, reduction of porosity.

question: Carbonate & Chemical Sediments & Diagenesis: key facts
answer: 2. Cementation: Precipitation of mineral matter (calcite, quartz, iron oxide) from pore fluids, binding grains.

question: Carbonate & Chemical Sediments & Diagenesis: key facts
answer: 3. Recrystallisation / Neomorphism: Unstable aragonite converts to stable calcite.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Basaltic / Mafic (45–52% SiO2)
answer: Low viscosity, high temp (1000–1200°C), dense, low gas. Minerals: Ca-rich plagioclase, augite, olivine. Extrusive: Basalt. Intrusive: Gabbro / Dolerite.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Andesitic / Intermediate (52–66% SiO2)
answer: Moderate viscosity & temp (800–1000°C). Minerals: Na-Ca plagioclase, hornblende, biotite. Extrusive: Andesite. Intrusive: Diorite.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Rhyolitic / Silicic / Felsic (>66% SiO2)
answer: High viscosity, lower temp (700–900°C), low density, volatile-rich (explosive). Minerals: Quartz, orthoclase, Na-plagioclase, muscovite/biotite. Extrusive: Rhyolite. Intrusive: Granite.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Equigranular / Phaneritic
answer: Coarse crystals (>1 mm), uniform slow cooling deep underground (e.g. granite, gabbro).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Aphanitic
answer: Fine crystals (<1 mm), rapid cooling at or near surface (e.g. basalt, rhyolite).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Porphyritic
answer: Two distinct crystal sizes: large phenocrysts formed during early slow cooling at depth, set in fine groundmass formed during rapid cooling upon ascent/eruption.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Glassy (Obsidian)
answer: Instantaneous quenching, no time for crystal lattice to form.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Vesicular & Amygdaloidal
answer: Gas bubbles trapped upon eruption (vesicles e.g. pumice, scoria); later filled by secondary minerals like calcite or quartz (amygdales).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Concordant intrusions
answer: Parallel to bedding. Sill: Chilled margins top and bottom; baked margins top and bottom; country rock xenoliths; no vesicles.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Extrusive lava flow
answer: Chilled margin only at base; baked margin only below; vesicular, weathered/eroded top; fragments incorporated into overlying sedimentary bed.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Discordant intrusions
answer: Cut across country rock. Dyke (steep tabular sheet), Pluton / Batholith (large discordant magma chamber >100 km²).

question: Contact (Thermal) Metamorphism: key facts
answer: High temperature, low pressure, isotropic (uniform) confining stress. Occurs in metamorphic aureole surrounding igneous intrusions.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Aureole zones in pelitic (shale/mudstone) host rock
Contact (Thermal) Metamorphism: key facts
answer: • Outer zone (lowest temp): Spotted slate / Spotted rock (incipient growth of biotite/cordierite clusters).

question: Contact (Thermal) Metamorphism: key facts
answer: • Middle zone: Andalusite hornfels (porphyroblasts of chiastolite with carbonaceous cross inclusions).

question: Contact (Thermal) Metamorphism: key facts
answer: • Inner zone (highest temp): Sillimanite-cordierite hornfels (dense, hard, granoblastic, non-foliated).

question: Contact (Thermal) Metamorphism: key facts
answer: Pure rocks: Limestone -> Marble (coarse granoblastic calcite); Sandstone -> Metaquartzite (interlocking quartz grains).

question: Regional Metamorphism & Foliation Sequence: key facts
answer: High directed stress + high confining pressure + elevated temperature. Convergent plate collisions / orogenesis.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Barrovian prograde metamorphic zones (pelite sequence)
Regional Metamorphism & Foliation Sequence: key facts
answer: 1. Slate: Microscopic platy minerals aligned perpendicular to maximum principal stress (\(\sigma_1\)) -> slaty cleavage.

question: Regional Metamorphism & Foliation Sequence: key facts
answer: 2. Phyllite: Fine white mica/chlorite gives a silky lustrous sheen; wavy foliation.

question: Regional Metamorphism & Foliation Sequence: key facts
answer: 3. Schist: Medium-coarse visible platy minerals (muscovite/biotite) forming continuous foliation (schistosity); contains porphyroblasts (garnet, staurolite).

question: Regional Metamorphism & Foliation Sequence: key facts
answer: 4. Gneiss: High-grade segregation into alternating light quartzo-feldspathic bands and dark mafic (biotite/hornblende) bands (gneissose banding).

question: Regional Metamorphism & Foliation Sequence: key facts
answer: 5. Migmatite: Partial melting of felsic components (anatexis) forming mixed metamorphic-igneous rock.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Strike
answer: The compass trend of a horizontal line on a dipping planar surface (e.g. 045°).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Dip
answer: The maximum angle of inclination measured perpendicular to strike downwards from the horizontal (e.g. 30° SE).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Apparent dip
answer: The inclination measured in any non-perpendicular direction to strike; always less than true dip.

question: Compare and distinguish: Brittle vs Ductile deformation
answer: Low temp/confining pressure + fast strain rate = brittle (faults/joints); High temp/pressure + slow strain rate = ductile (folding/ductile shear).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Anticline
answer: Convex upwards fold with oldest strata in core.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Syncline
answer: Concave upwards fold with youngest strata in core.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Symmetrical fold
answer: Axial plane is vertical; limbs dip in opposite directions at equal angles.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Asymmetrical fold
answer: Axial plane is inclined; limbs dip at different angles.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Overturned fold
answer: One limb is tilted beyond vertical so strata are inverted (younger below older).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Recumbent fold
answer: Axial plane is horizontal or sub-horizontal (dip <10°).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Plunging fold
answer: Fold hinge line is inclined to the horizontal; produces V-shaped or U-shaped outcrop pattern on flat terrain. Anticlines plunge towards the closed apex of the V; synclines plunge towards the open end.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Normal fault
answer: Extensional stress (\(\sigma_1\) vertical). Hanging wall moves down relative to footwall. Lengthens crust. Omits strata on maps.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Reverse fault
answer: Compressional stress (\(\sigma_1\) horizontal). Hanging wall moves up relative to footwall (dip >45°). Shortens crust. Duplicates strata.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Thrust fault
answer: Low-angle reverse fault (dip <45°); places older rocks over younger rocks over large lateral distances.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Strike-slip (tear) fault
answer: Shear stress (\(\sigma_2\) vertical). Lateral displacement (dextral = clockwise/right-lateral; sinistral = anticlockwise/left-lateral).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Field & map evidence for faulting
answer: Truncation and offset of beds, slickensides (grooves showing movement direction), fault breccia / fault gouge, drag folds (limbs flexed towards fault movement), spring lines.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Angular unconformity
answer: Gap in geological record where tilted/folded older rocks are eroded and overlain by flatter younger rocks.

question: Unconformities & The Rule of V's: key facts
answer: • Evidence: Truncation of beds below, dip discordance, basal conglomerate containing pebbles derived from underlying unit.

question: State the principle/formula for: Rule of V's (Map Outcrop Pattern across Valleys)
Unconformities & The Rule of V's: key facts
answer: • Horizontal beds: Contour parallel; outcrop bands follow contours.

question: Unconformities & The Rule of V's: key facts
answer: • Vertical beds: Straight lines across topography regardless of valleys/hills.

question: Unconformities & The Rule of V's: key facts
answer: • Dipping beds: V points in the direction of dip down a valley, UNLESS the bed dips downstream at a lower angle than the valley gradient.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Fossil
answer: Any preserved remains, impression, or trace of organisms from past geological ages.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Favourable preservation factors
answer: Hard skeleton/shell (calcite, silica, apatite), rapid burial (prevents scavenging and mechanical destruction), low energy environment, anoxic bottom waters (inhibits bacterial decay).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Preservation modes
Fossil Preservation & Taphonomy: key facts
answer: • Replacement / Petrifaction: Original mineral replaced molecule by molecule (e.g. pyritisation, silicification).

question: Fossil Preservation & Taphonomy: key facts
answer: • Recrystallisation: Unstable aragonite converts to coarse calcite crystals.

question: Fossil Preservation & Taphonomy: key facts
answer: • Moulds & Casts: Shell dissolves leaving external mould (impressing wall) and internal mould (steinkern); infilled with sediment/mineral = cast.

question: Fossil Preservation & Taphonomy: key facts
answer: • Carbonisation: Volatiles expelled leaving thin black carbon film (plants, graptolites).

question: Fossil Preservation & Taphonomy: key facts
answer: • Trace fossils (ichnofossils): Tracks, trails, burrows, coprolites, borings; classify behavior (feeding, dwelling, resting, locomotion).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Life Assemblage (In Situ / Biocoenosis)
Life Assemblage vs Death Assemblage: key facts
answer: • Organisms preserved in living position (e.g. upright corals, bivalves in burrows).

question: Life Assemblage vs Death Assemblage: key facts
answer: • Articulated multi-part skeletons (complete trilobites with free cheeks attached; bivalves with valves closed).

question: Life Assemblage vs Death Assemblage: key facts
answer: • Wide size distribution / growth stages (juveniles and adults together).

question: Life Assemblage vs Death Assemblage: key facts
answer: • Unbroken, unworn delicate spines/frills preserved.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Death Assemblage (Transported / Thanatocoenosis)
Life Assemblage vs Death Assemblage: key facts
answer: • Disarticulated valves/segments (isolated bivalve valves, separated trilobite cranidia/pygidia).

question: Life Assemblage vs Death Assemblage: key facts
answer: • Hydrodynamically sorted (all shells same size/weight).

question: Life Assemblage vs Death Assemblage: key facts
answer: • Broken, abraded, rounded shell fragments.

question: Life Assemblage vs Death Assemblage: key facts
answer: • Current alignment of elongate fossils (graptolites, belemnites, tentaculites).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Trilobites (Arthropods, Cambrian–Permian)
answer: Cephalon (head), thorax (segmented), pygidium (tail). Glabella, compound eyes, facial sutures. Pelagic/swimmer (huge eyes, streamlined), Benthic crawler (medium eyes, sturdy legs), Burrower (no eyes, spade-shaped cephalon).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Brachiopods (Cambrian–Recent)
answer: Bilateral symmetry perpendicular to hinge line (plane cuts through middle of both valves). Pedicle valve larger with pedicle foramen (anchored to sea floor), brachial valve supports lophophore filter-feeding organ.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Bivalves (Molluscs, Cambrian–Recent)
answer: Bilateral symmetry between the two valves (valves are mirror images of each other). Pallial sinus presence = deep burrower with retractable siphons; thick ribbed shell = high energy shallow marine.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Corals (Cnidarians)
answer: Calcareous skeleton (corallite), septa (radiating radial plates), tabulae (horizontal floor plates). Solitary (horn corals e.g. Zaphrentis) vs colonial. Shallow, warm (>20°C), clear, agitated, normal marine salinity reef environments.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Graptolites (Hemichordates, Cambrian–Devonian)
answer: Planktonic colonial organisms. Stipes composed of thecae housing zooids. Rapid morphological evolution: Ordovician multi-stiped pendent/horizontal -> Silurian single-stiped scandent (Monograptus). Excellent zone fossils for deep marine shales.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Law of Superposition
answer: In undeformed sedimentary/volcanic sequence, oldest bed at bottom, youngest at top.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Principle of Original Horizontality
answer: Sediments are deposited under gravity in flat, horizontal layers; tilting/folding occurred post-deposition.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Cross-cutting relationships
answer: Any feature (fault, igneous intrusion, mineral vein, unconformity) that cuts across another rock unit is younger than the rock it cuts.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Principle of Inclusions
answer: Fragments (xenoliths in igneous rocks; pebbles in conglomerates) are always older than the rock containing them.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Sedimentary way-up
answer: Cross-bedding truncation (eroded at top), Graded bedding (coarse at bottom, fine at top), Ripple crests (point up), Mudcracks (V points down), Flute casts/load casts (bulbous downward projections on bed base).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Volcanic way-up
answer: Pillow lavas (convex rounded top, cusped/keeled base fitting into underlying pillow), baked margin on bottom of flow only, vesicular zone at flow top.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Paleontological way-up
answer: Plant roots branching downwards; corals growing upright.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Characteristics of an ideal Index / Zone Fossil
Biostratigraphy & Ideal Zone Fossils: key facts
answer: 1. Rapid evolution: Short stratigraphic range (precise dating).

question: Biostratigraphy & Ideal Zone Fossils: key facts
answer: 2. Geographically widespread: Found across basins and continents.

question: Biostratigraphy & Ideal Zone Fossils: key facts
answer: 3. Abundant: Easily found in rock exposures and drill cores.

question: Biostratigraphy & Ideal Zone Fossils: key facts
answer: 4. Easily identifiable: Distinct morphological features.

question: Biostratigraphy & Ideal Zone Fossils: key facts
answer: 5. Facies-independent: Pelagic / planktonic (floated in water column, found in many sediment types).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Best index fossils
answer: Graptolites (Ordovician–Silurian), Ammonites (Devonian–Cretaceous), Microfossils/Conodonts/Foraminifera (Phanerozoic).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Radioactive decay
answer: Unstable parent isotope decays to stable radiogenic daughter isotope at a constant exponential rate unaffected by heat, pressure, or chemistry.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Half-life (t1/2)
answer: Time taken for half the radioactive parent atoms to decay.

question: Radiometric Absolute Dating: key facts
Explain the key features / significance of: Closure temperature
answer: The temperature below which isotopes can no longer diffuse out of the crystal lattice. If rock is reheated during metamorphism above closure temp, radiogenic daughter escapes and radiometric clock is reset.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Key isotope systems
Radiometric Absolute Dating: key facts
answer: • K-Ar / Ar-Ar: K-40 decays to Ar-40 (t1/2 = 1.25 Ga). Dating igneous/metamorphic biotite, hornblende, sanidine.

question: Radiometric Absolute Dating: key facts
answer: • U-Pb: U-238/U-235 in Zircon. Zircon has very high closure temp (>900°C), retains primary crystallisation age.

question: Radiometric Absolute Dating: key facts
answer: • Carbon-14: t1/2 = 5,730 yrs. Only dates organic material up to ~50,000 years (Quaternary).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: P-waves (Primary / Compressional)
answer: Longitudinal particle motion parallel to wave propagation. Travel through solids and liquids. Fastest wave (~6–13 km/s).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: S-waves (Secondary / Shear)
answer: Transverse particle motion perpendicular to wave propagation. Shear elastic resistance only. Cannot travel through liquids or gases (velocity drops to zero). Slower than P-waves (~3.5–7 km/s).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Ray Paths & Velocity
answer: In a homogeneous solid, velocity increases with depth due to rising rigidity and incompressibility exceeding density increase -> seismic rays refract/bend upwards.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Moho (Mohorovičić Discontinuity)
answer: Crust-mantle boundary. P-wave velocity jumps abruptly from ~6.0 km/s (crust) to ~8.0 km/s (peridotite mantle).

question: Earth's Internal Discontinuities & Layers: key facts
answer: • Continental crust: 30–70 km thick, granitic/felsic, density ~2.7 g/cm³.

question: Earth's Internal Discontinuities & Layers: key facts
answer: • Oceanic crust: 5–10 km thick, basaltic/gabbroic, density ~3.0 g/cm³.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Low Velocity Zone (LVZ / Asthenosphere)
answer: Depth 100–250 km. P and S velocities dip slightly due to 1–2% partial melting; ductile, allows tectonic plate movement.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Gutenberg Discontinuity (Core-Mantle Boundary / CMB, 2900 km)
Earth's Internal Discontinuities & Layers: key facts
answer: • P-wave velocity drops sharply from ~13.7 km/s to ~8.1 km/s.

question: Earth's Internal Discontinuities & Layers: key facts
answer: • S-wave velocity drops to zero -> proves the outer core is liquid.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Lehmann Discontinuity (Inner Core Boundary, 5150 km)
answer: P-wave velocity jumps from ~10.3 km/s to ~11.2 km/s -> confirms solid inner core (high pressure prevents melting).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: P-wave shadow zone (103° to 142°)
answer: Caused by severe refraction (bending inwards) of P-waves entering the slower liquid outer core at the Gutenberg discontinuity.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: S-wave shadow zone (103° to 180°)
answer: Complete absence of direct S-waves beyond 103° on either side of earthquake focus because S-waves cannot travel through the liquid outer core.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Isostasy
answer: Gravitational equilibrium between Earth's lithosphere floating on the denser asthenosphere.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Airy hypothesis
answer: Uniform crustal density, varying root depth (tall mountains have deep buoyant crustal roots).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Post-glacial rebound
answer: Melting of continental ice sheets causes lithosphere to slowly uplift as asthenosphere flows back in.

question: What is the Evidence for drift?
answer: Continental shelf jigsaw fit, matching fossil distributions (Glossopteris flora, Mesosaurus), matching mountain belts across Atlantic, late Paleozoic glacial striations and tillites across southern continents (Gondwana).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Remanent Magnetism
answer: As mafic lava cools below the Curie point of magnetite (~580°C), magnetic dipoles align with Earth's current magnetic field and lock in.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Seafloor Spreading (Vine-Matthews-Morley)
answer: Symmetrical marine magnetic anomalies ('stripes' of normal and reversed polarities) parallel to mid-ocean ridges. Ocean crust age increases symmetrically away from ridge axis.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Divergent (Constructive)
answer: Decompression melting of asthenospheric mantle -> basaltic volcanism, pillow lavas, sheeted dykes, normal fault grabens, shallow earthquakes (e.g. Mid-Atlantic Ridge, East African Rift).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Convergent (Destructive) - Ocean/Continent (Andean)
Plate Boundaries & Characteristic Features: key facts
answer: • Subducting slab creates deep ocean trench and Benioff zone (earthquakes from shallow to deep down to 700 km).

question: Plate Boundaries & Characteristic Features: key facts
answer: • Flux melting (water released by dehydration of slab lowers mantle solidus) produces intermediate andesitic/dacitic arc volcanism.

question: Plate Boundaries & Characteristic Features: key facts
answer: • Accretionary wedge of scraped-off sediments.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Convergent - Continent/Continent (Himalayan)
answer: Intense crustal shortening, folding, reverse/thrust faults, regional metamorphism, high mountain plateau, no volcanism, shallow/intermediate earthquakes.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Conservative / Transform
answer: Lateral displacement, strike-slip faulting, shallow earthquakes, no volcanism (e.g. San Andreas Fault).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Slab Pull
answer: Cold, dense, subducted oceanic lithosphere undergoes eclogite metamorphism (very dense), sinking into asthenosphere under gravity and pulling the rest of the plate behind it. Dominant driving force (>90%).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Ridge Push
answer: Gravitational sliding of elevated, buoyant newly formed oceanic crust at mid-ocean ridge downslope away from the ridge axis.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Basal Drag
answer: Minor traction from mantle convection currents dragging base of lithospheric plate.

question: Hotspots & Mantle Plumes: key facts
answer: Stationary thermal upwellings originating from core-mantle boundary (D'' layer).

question: Hotspots & Mantle Plumes: key facts
answer: As tectonic plate moves over the fixed hotspot, a linear chain of volcanoes forms with progressive age increase away from the active volcanic centre (e.g. Hawaiian-Emperor seamount chain).

question: Hotspots & Mantle Plumes: key facts
answer: Direction of plate motion is towards the oldest volcano; rate of plate motion = distance / age difference.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Decompression melting
answer: Upward movement of solid mantle peridotite without loss of heat (adiabatic) crosses solidus. Occurs at mid-ocean ridges and hotspots.

question: State the principle/formula for: Flux melting (hydration)
answer: Subducting oceanic slab dewaters (serpentinite/clays break down); water enters overlying mantle wedge, lowering solidus temperature below ambient temperature. Occurs at subduction zones.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Thermal melting
answer: Conductive heat transfer from hot basaltic magma underplating crust melts continental crust.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Fractional crystallisation / Crystal settling
answer: Early-formed dense mafic minerals (olivine, Ca-plagioclase, pyroxene) settle out of liquid under gravity, depleting magma in Mg, Fe, Ca and enriching remaining liquid in Si, Na, K.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Crustal assimilation
answer: Hot rising magma melts and incorporates wall rock (xenolith digestion), shifting magma towards more silicic composition.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Magma mixing
answer: Influx of primitive mafic magma into evolving silicic chamber creates intermediate hybrids with mixed phenocrysts (e.g. resorbed quartz beside calcic plagioclase).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Liquid immiscibility
answer: Magma splits into two unmixable liquids (e.g. sulfide-rich melt and silicate-rich melt).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Binary Eutectic System (e.g. Diopside-Anorthite)
Phase Diagrams & The Lever Rule: key facts
answer: • Liquidus: Curve above which system is completely liquid.

question: Phase Diagrams & The Lever Rule: key facts
answer: • Solidus: Line below which system is completely solid.

question: Phase Diagrams & The Lever Rule: key facts
answer: • Eutectic point: Minimum melting temperature where liquid and both solid phases coexist at equilibrium. Final liquid always crystallises at eutectic composition.

question: State the principle/formula for: Lever Rule calculation
answer: Ratio of solid to liquid at any temperature: \(\% 	ext{Solid} =  rac{	ext{Distance to Liquidus}}{	ext{Total tie-line width}} 	imes 100\).

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Zeolite & Prehnite-Pumpellyite
answer: Low P, low T; burial metamorphism.

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Greenschist
answer: Moderate P, moderate T (300–450°C). Key minerals: Chlorite, actinolite, albite, epidote.

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Amphibolite
answer: Moderate-high P, high T (500–700°C). Key minerals: Hornblende, plagioclase, garnet, staurolite.

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Granulite
answer: High T (>750°C), anhydrous, deep continental crust. Key minerals: Pyroxene, sillimanite, garnet, perthitic feldspar.

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Blueschist
answer: High P, low T. Subducting slab at ocean trenches. Key diagnostic mineral: Glaucophane (blue sodic amphibole).

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Eclogite
answer: Ultra-high P, high T. Deeply subducted crust. Key minerals: Omphacite (green sodic pyroxene) + Pyrope garnet (pink).

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Porphyroblastic & Poikiloblastic
answer: Large metamorphic crystals (e.g. garnet, staurolite, andalusite) containing inclusions of earlier matrix minerals (sieve texture).

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Helicitic / Snowball Garnet
answer: Sigmoidal spiral trails of quartz inclusions inside garnet prove crystal rotated during ductile shear (syn-tectonic growth).

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Mylonites
answer: Intense ductile grain-size reduction in shear zones. Features: Ribbon quartz, dynamically recrystallised mortar texture.

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Rotated Porphyroclasts

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Microtextures & Shear-Sense Indicators: key facts
answer: • Sigma (\(\sigma\)) clasts: Tails / wings extend symmetrically into foliation; indicate shear sense.

topicTitle: Topic G1.2 · Metamorphic Rocks: Mineralogy & Texture
question: Microtextures & Shear-Sense Indicators: key facts
answer: • Delta (\(\delta\)) clasts: Tails curved and wrapped around porphyroclast from significant rotation.

question: Bouma Sequence (Turbidite Deposition): key facts
answer: Formed by decelerating subaqueous density flow in deep marine environment.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Ta division
answer: Massive to normally graded coarse sandstone/gravel, sharp erosive base with sole marks (flute casts, groove casts).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Tb division
answer: Parallel plane-laminated sandstone (upper flow regime flat bed).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Tc division
answer: Ripple cross-laminated or climbing ripple sandstone/siltstone with convolute lamination (lower flow regime).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Td division
answer: Parallel laminated siltstone.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Te division
answer: Structureless hemipelagic clay/mud.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Paleocurrent measurements
answer: Flute casts, cross-bed dips, ripple crests, parting lineations.

question: Paleocurrent Vector Mean & Distributions: key facts
answer: • Unimodal distribution (rose diagram with one strong direction): Fluvial / river channel or delta.

question: Paleocurrent Vector Mean & Distributions: key facts
answer: • Bimodal / bipolar distribution (two opposite peaks 180° apart): Tidal marine shelf (flood and ebb tides).

question: Paleocurrent Vector Mean & Distributions: key facts
answer: • Polymodal / random: Deep ocean pelagic or aeolian variable dune.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Stress
answer: Force applied per unit area. Three mutually perpendicular principal stress axes: \(\sigma_1\) (maximum), \(\sigma_2\) (intermediate), \(\sigma_3\) (minimum).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Strain
answer: Deformation/distortion of rock body resulting from applied stress. Strain ellipsoid axes: \(X \ge Y \ge Z\).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Flinn Diagram
answer: Plots strain ratio \(a = X/Y\) vs \(b = Y/Z\).

question: Stress & Strain Ellipsoids: key facts
answer: • \(k > 1\): Constrictional strain (prolate 'cigar' shape, e.g. pencil cleavage).

question: Stress & Strain Ellipsoids: key facts
answer: • \(k = 1\): Plane strain (no volume change in Y).

question: Stress & Strain Ellipsoids: key facts
answer: • \(k < 1\): Flattening strain (oblate 'pancake' shape, e.g. slaty cleavage).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Pressure solution
answer: Dissolution of minerals at high-stress grain contacts and precipitation in low-stress shadows (forms stylolites in limestones).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Dislocation creep / Plastic glide
answer: Movement of crystal lattice imperfections; dynamic recrystallisation.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Stereonet interpretation
answer: Poles to bedding planes plotted on equal-area stereonet lie along a great circle (the \(\pi\)-girdle); the pole to this girdle defines the trend and plunge of the fold axis.

topicTitle: Topic G3.1 · Fossils & Diversity of Life
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Phyletic gradualism
answer: Slow, steady, continuous transformation of lineages over geological time.

topicTitle: Topic G3.1 · Fossils & Diversity of Life
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Punctuated equilibrium
answer: Long periods of morphological stasis interrupted by rapid speciation events in small isolated populations.

topicTitle: Topic G3.1 · Fossils & Diversity of Life
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Adaptive radiation
answer: Rapid diversification of an ancestral group into many ecological niches following evolutionary novelty or mass extinction opening up vacant ecospace.

topicTitle: Topic G3.1 · Fossils & Diversity of Life
question: Explain the key features / significance of: 1. End-Ordovician (~444 Ma)
answer: Glaciation on Gondwana, eustatic sea-level drop, loss of shallow marine shelf habitat.

topicTitle: Topic G3.1 · Fossils & Diversity of Life
question: Explain the key features / significance of: 2. Late Devonian (~375 Ma)
answer: Oceanic anoxia, cooling; hit shallow benthic corals/brachiopods.

topicTitle: Topic G3.1 · Fossils & Diversity of Life
question: Explain the key features / significance of: 3. End-Permian ('The Great Dying', ~252 Ma)
answer: Largest extinction in history (~96% marine species, ~70% terrestrial vertebrates lost).

topicTitle: Topic G3.1 · Fossils & Diversity of Life
question: The Big Five Mass Extinctions: key facts
answer: • Causes: Siberian Traps flood basalt volcanism releasing massive CO2 and SO2 -> global warming, ocean acidification, widespread marine anoxia, ozone layer destruction.

topicTitle: Topic G3.1 · Fossils & Diversity of Life
question: Explain the key features / significance of: 4. End-Triassic (~201 Ma)
answer: Central Atlantic Magmatic Province (CAMP) rifting; paved way for dinosaur dominance.

topicTitle: Topic G3.1 · Fossils & Diversity of Life
question: Explain the key features / significance of: 5. End-Cretaceous (K-Pg, ~66 Ma)
answer: Non-avian dinosaurs, ammonites, marine reptiles extinct.

topicTitle: Topic G3.1 · Fossils & Diversity of Life
question: The Big Five Mass Extinctions: key facts
answer: • Causes: Chicxulub bolide impact (Iridium anomaly in boundary clay, shocked quartz, tektites/microkrystites, tsunami deposits) combined with Deccan Traps volcanism.

topicTitle: Topic G3.2 · Factors in Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Orbital Eccentricity (100,000 & 400,000 yr)
answer: Earth's orbit cycles between circular and elliptical, altering total incoming solar radiation.

topicTitle: Topic G3.2 · Factors in Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Obliquity / Axial Tilt (41,000 yr)
answer: Tilt cycles between 22.1° and 24.5° (currently 23.4°). Greater tilt = more extreme seasons (warmer summers, colder winters). Less tilt favours ice sheet growth as mild summers fail to melt winter snow.

topicTitle: Topic G3.2 · Factors in Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Precession of Equinoxes (21,000–26,000 yr)
answer: Wobble of Earth's rotational axis; alters timing of seasons relative to perihelion.

topicTitle: Topic G3.2 · Factors in Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Continental position
answer: Landmasses over poles allow ice sheet buildup (e.g. Antarctica in Cenozoic).

topicTitle: Topic G3.2 · Factors in Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Oceanic gateways
answer: Opening of Drake Passage separated South America from Antarctica -> Antarctic Circumpolar Current thermally isolated Antarctica, initiating continental glaciation (~34 Ma).

topicTitle: Topic G3.2 · Factors in Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Mountain uplift & CO2 drawdown
answer: Himalayan collision exposed vast silicate rocks; intense chemical weathering (hydrolysis) drew down atmospheric CO2, driving global Cenozoic cooling.

topicTitle: Topic G3.3 · Evidence for Climate Change
question: Oxygen Isotopes (d18O) as Paleothermometers: key facts
answer: 16O (light) evaporates preferentially over 18O (heavy).

topicTitle: Topic G3.3 · Evidence for Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: During Glacial / Icehouse Periods

topicTitle: Topic G3.3 · Evidence for Climate Change
question: Oxygen Isotopes (d18O) as Paleothermometers: key facts
answer: • Light 16O evaporates, falls as snow, and is trapped in continental ice sheets.

topicTitle: Topic G3.3 · Evidence for Climate Change
question: Oxygen Isotopes (d18O) as Paleothermometers: key facts
answer: • Ice cores have negative \(\delta^{18} ext{O}\) (depleted in 18O).

topicTitle: Topic G3.3 · Evidence for Climate Change
question: Oxygen Isotopes (d18O) as Paleothermometers: key facts
answer: • Oceans become enriched in 18O -> marine foraminifera shells have positive \(\delta^{18} ext{O}\).

topicTitle: Topic G3.3 · Evidence for Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: During Interglacial Periods
answer: Melting ice returns 16O to oceans; marine carbonate \(\delta^{18}	ext{O}\) decreases.

topicTitle: Topic G3.3 · Evidence for Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Glacial
answer: Tillites / diamictites (unsorted, striated clasts), dropstones deforming laminations in marine shale.

topicTitle: Topic G3.3 · Evidence for Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Arid / Desert
answer: Aeolian dunes (large-scale cross-bedding), red beds (hematite coating), evaporites (halite, gypsum).

topicTitle: Topic G3.3 · Evidence for Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Humid / Tropical
answer: Thick coal beds (warm swamps), laterites/bauxites (leached tropical soils).

topicTitle: Topic G3.3 · Evidence for Climate Change
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Foraminiferal coiling
answer: Neogloboquadrina pachyderma coils to the left (sinistral) in polar water (<7°C) and to the right (dextral) in warmer waters.

topicTitle: Topic G4.1 · Concentration of Natural Resources
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Magmatic segregation / Immiscibility
answer: Dense sulfide or oxide liquids separate from mafic magma and sink to base of intrusion (e.g. Bushveld chromite, Sudbury Ni-Cu).

topicTitle: Topic G4.1 · Concentration of Natural Resources
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Hydrothermal veins
answer: Superheated volatile-rich aqueous fluids scavenge metals from cooling plutons and country rocks, precipitating ore minerals in fracture veins as pressure and temperature drop.

topicTitle: Topic G4.1 · Concentration of Natural Resources
question: Magmatic & Hydrothermal Ore Deposits: key facts
answer: • Mineral zoning away from granite intrusion: Sn (cassiterite) & W (wolframite) closest (highest T) -> Cu (chalcopyrite) -> Zn (sphalerite) -> Pb (galena) -> Fe (pyrite) furthest.

topicTitle: Topic G4.1 · Concentration of Natural Resources
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Porphyry deposits
answer: Massive low-grade copper/molybdenum deposits associated with subduction arc plutons; pervasive stockwork veinlet network.

topicTitle: Topic G4.1 · Concentration of Natural Resources
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Placer deposits
answer: Mechanical concentration by fluvial/coastal currents.

topicTitle: Topic G4.1 · Concentration of Natural Resources
question: Placer & Residual Deposits: key facts
answer: • Requires minerals that are: Dense (high relative density), Chemically inert (resistant to weathering), and Mechanically hard (resist abrasion).

topicTitle: Topic G4.1 · Concentration of Natural Resources
question: Placer & Residual Deposits: key facts
answer: • Examples: Native Gold (RD 19.3), Diamond (H 10), Cassiterite (SnO2, RD 7.0), Magnetite, Zircon.

topicTitle: Topic G4.1 · Concentration of Natural Resources
question: Placer & Residual Deposits: key facts
answer: • Concentrated at inside of meander bends, downstream of confluences, behind rock bars, and plunge pools.

topicTitle: Topic G4.1 · Concentration of Natural Resources
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Residual deposits (Bauxite & Kaolinite)

topicTitle: Topic G4.1 · Concentration of Natural Resources
question: Placer & Residual Deposits: key facts
answer: • Bauxite (Al ore): Extreme tropical weathering leaches silica, leaving insoluble hydrous aluminium oxides (gibbsite).

topicTitle: Topic G4.1 · Concentration of Natural Resources
question: Placer & Residual Deposits: key facts
answer: • Kaolinite (China clay): Hydrothermal or deep weathering breakdown of feldspar in granites.

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: The Petroleum System (Five Essentials): key facts
answer: 1. Source Rock: Organic-rich (sapropelic) marine mudstone/shale with >1% Total Organic Carbon (TOC). Plankton buried in anoxic conditions.

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: The Petroleum System (Five Essentials): key facts
answer: 2. Maturation: Thermal cooking under burial:

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: The Petroleum System (Five Essentials): key facts
answer: • Oil Window: 60°C to 120°C (burial depth 2–4 km).

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: The Petroleum System (Five Essentials): key facts
answer: • Gas Window: 120°C to 200°C (burial depth 4–6 km).

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: The Petroleum System (Five Essentials): key facts
answer: • Above 200°C: Over-mature; hydrocarbons graphitised/destroyed.

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: The Petroleum System (Five Essentials): key facts
answer: 3. Reservoir Rock: Porous (stores fluids) and permeable (allows extraction). E.g. well-sorted sandstone, oolitic/reefal limestone.

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: The Petroleum System (Five Essentials): key facts
answer: 4. Cap Rock (Seal): Impermeable rock barrier preventing escape. E.g. thick shale, mudstone, or evaporites (halite/anhydrite).

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: The Petroleum System (Five Essentials): key facts
answer: 5. Trap: Geometric arrangement halting migration:

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: The Petroleum System (Five Essentials): key facts
answer: • Structural: Anticlinal crest, fault trap (reservoir juxtaposed against impermeable shale), salt dome/diapir.

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: The Petroleum System (Five Essentials): key facts
answer: • Stratigraphic: Unconformity trap, sand pinch-out / lens, reef buildup.

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Porosity
answer: Volume of pore space as percentage of total rock volume: \(\phi =  rac{V_{	ext{void}}}{V_{	ext{total}}} 	imes 100\).

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Permeability
answer: Interconnectedness of pores allowing fluid flow.

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Coalification Rank
answer: Progressive increase in burial T, P, and time:

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: Hydraulic Properties & Coal Series: key facts
answer: • Peat -> Lignite (brown coal) -> Bituminous coal (lustrous, black) -> Anthracite (hard, shiny, non-smudge).

topicTitle: Topic G4.2 · Oil, Gas & Coal Formation
question: Hydraulic Properties & Coal Series: key facts
answer: • Trend: Carbon content increases (up to 95%), calorific value increases, moisture and volatile content decrease.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Gravity survey (Gravimeter)
answer: Measures local variations in gravitational field (\(g\)).

question: Geophysical Exploration Methods: key facts
answer: • Positive anomaly (gravity high): Dense subsurface bodies (massive metallic sulfide ore bodies, mafic/ultramafic intrusions).

question: Geophysical Exploration Methods: key facts
answer: • Negative anomaly (gravity low): Low-density bodies (salt domes, granite plutons, sedimentary basins, caverns).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Magnetic survey (Magnetometer)
answer: Detects variations in Earth's magnetic field due to magnetic minerals (magnetite, pyrrhotite).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Seismic reflection
answer: Generates acoustic waves; reflected at boundaries between rocks of differing acoustic impedance (\(Z = ho imes v\)). Produces cross-sectional profiles of subsurface structures and traps.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Geochemical survey
answer: Systematically samples soil, stream sediments, or water to identify anomalous concentrations above regional background levels.

question: Geochemical Prospecting & Borehole Logging: key facts
answer: • Contour maps plotted with isolines (e.g. 50 ppm, 100 ppm Cu); highest values pinpoint upstream or upslope ore subcrop.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Borehole geophysical logging
Geochemical Prospecting & Borehole Logging: key facts
answer: • Gamma log: Measures natural radioactivity. High gamma = shale/clay (rich in K-40); Low gamma = sandstone, limestone, evaporites.

question: Geochemical Prospecting & Borehole Logging: key facts
answer: • Resistivity log: High resistivity = hydrocarbons or fresh water; Low resistivity = saline formation water in pores.

question: Geochemical Prospecting & Borehole Logging: key facts
answer: • Sonic log: Measures seismic velocity to calculate porosity.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Earthquake hazards
answer: Ground shaking, liquefaction (water-saturated unconsolidated sand behaves as liquid), landslides, tsunamis.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Volcanic prediction precursors
Seismic Hazards & Volcanic Monitoring: key facts
answer: • Harmonic volcanic tremor and shallow earthquake swarms (magma moving through conduits).

question: Seismic Hazards & Volcanic Monitoring: key facts
answer: • Ground deformation: Tiltmeters, GPS, and satellite InSAR detect swelling / inflation of volcanic edifice.

question: Seismic Hazards & Volcanic Monitoring: key facts
answer: • Gas emissions: Increasing SO2 and CO2 emission rates and ratios.

question: Seismic Hazards & Volcanic Monitoring: key facts
answer: • Thermal anomalies: FLIR infrared imaging detects rising magma.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Factor of Safety (\(F\))
answer: \(F =  rac{\sum 	ext{Resisting Forces}}{\sum 	ext{Driving Forces}}\). If \(F > 1\) slope is stable; \(F < 1\) failure occurs.

question: Slope Stability & Engineering Geology: key facts
answer: • Driving forces: Gravity component parallel to slope, slope surcharge (buildings).

question: Slope Stability & Engineering Geology: key facts
answer: • Resisting forces: Cohesion, friction across potential slip planes.

question: Slope Stability & Engineering Geology: key facts
answer: • Pore water pressure: Reduces effective normal stress across slip planes, triggering landslides.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Engineering mitigation
answer: Horizontal drainage pipes (relieves pore pressure), rock bolts (pins beds together across dip), retaining walls with weep holes, gabion baskets, shotcrete.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Strike lines (structural contours)
answer: Straight lines connecting points of equal elevation on a planar geological surface (bedding plane or fault).

question: Three-Point Problems & Strike Lines: key facts
answer: • The direction of a strike line is the strike of the bed.

question: Three-Point Problems & Strike Lines: key facts
answer: • Spacing between strike lines indicates dip: closer lines = steeper dip; wider lines = gentler dip.

question: State the principle/formula for: Dip calculation from strike lines
answer: \(	an(	ext{Dip}) =  rac{	ext{Contour Interval}}{	ext{Horizontal Distance between strike lines}}\).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Glacial erosional landforms
answer: Corries/cirques with tarns, arêtes, pyramidal peaks, U-shaped glacial troughs, hanging valleys, roche moutonnées (smooth plucked stoss-and-lee).

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Glacial depositional landforms
answer: Moraines (terminal, lateral, medial, recessional), drumlins (streamlined elongate hills, steep blunt stoss end points up-ice), erratics, kettle holes.

question: Explain the key features / significance of: Periglacial landforms
answer: Permafrost and active layer; solifluction/gelifluction sheets; patterned ground (stone polygons sorted by frost heave); ice wedges and fossil ice wedge pseudomorphs (prove continuous permafrost).

category: Terranes & Orogenic Cycles of the British Isles
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Caledonian Orogeny (Ordovician–Devonian)
answer: Closure of Iapetus Ocean; Laurentia (Scotland & NW Ireland) collided with Eastern Avalonia (England & Wales). Marked by the Iapetus Suture zone.

category: Terranes & Orogenic Cycles of the British Isles
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Variscan Orogeny (Carboniferous–Permian)
answer: Closure of Rheic Ocean; collision of Armorica/Gondwana with Euramerica to assemble Pangaea. Intense folding in SW England (Cornubian batholith emplacement).

category: Terranes & Orogenic Cycles of the British Isles
question: Explain the key features / significance of: Northward Drift of Britain

category: Terranes & Orogenic Cycles of the British Isles
question: Terranes & Orogenic Cycles of the British Isles: key facts
answer: • Cambrian: ~60°S (cold seas).

category: Terranes & Orogenic Cycles of the British Isles
question: Terranes & Orogenic Cycles of the British Isles: key facts
answer: • Carboniferous: Equatorial ~0° (warm tropical coal-forming swamps).

category: Terranes & Orogenic Cycles of the British Isles
question: Terranes & Orogenic Cycles of the British Isles: key facts
answer: • Permian–Triassic: 10°–20°N (arid trade wind desert, New Red Sandstone).

category: Terranes & Orogenic Cycles of the British Isles
question: Terranes & Orogenic Cycles of the British Isles: key facts
answer: • Present: ~54°N (temperate).

topicTitle: Theme T5 · Geology of the Lithosphere
question: Ophiolite Complex (Oceanic Lithosphere Section): key facts
answer: Complete preserved section of oceanic crust and upper mantle obducted onto land.

topicTitle: Theme T5 · Geology of the Lithosphere
question: Ophiolite Complex (Oceanic Lithosphere Section): key facts
answer: 1. Pelagic sediment: Deep-sea chert, black mudstone, siliceous ooze (top).

topicTitle: Theme T5 · Geology of the Lithosphere
question: Ophiolite Complex (Oceanic Lithosphere Section): key facts
answer: 2. Pillow basalts: Extrusive lavas quenched in seawater.

topicTitle: Theme T5 · Geology of the Lithosphere
question: Ophiolite Complex (Oceanic Lithosphere Section): key facts
answer: 3. Sheeted dyke complex: Sub-vertical feeder dykes formed in 100% extensional spreading zone.

topicTitle: Theme T5 · Geology of the Lithosphere
question: Ophiolite Complex (Oceanic Lithosphere Section): key facts
answer: 4. Gabbro: Coarse-grained, isotropic at top, layered cumulate at base.

topicTitle: Theme T5 · Geology of the Lithosphere
question: Ophiolite Complex (Oceanic Lithosphere Section): key facts
answer: 5. Moho Discontinuity: Petrographic boundary between gabbro and peridotite.

topicTitle: Theme T5 · Geology of the Lithosphere
question: Ophiolite Complex (Oceanic Lithosphere Section): key facts
answer: 6. Ultramafic mantle: Harzburgite / lherzolite, often altered to serpentinite.
